title: Biochemistry — Mixed Exam Formats (DOMiNANCE Originals)
source: KNUST Biochemistry lectures and corresponding study guides

questions.stem:
Assertion: Vitamin K deficiency may cause bleeding.
Reason: Gamma-carboxylation permits clotting factors to bind calcium.
questions.why: Vitamin K supports gamma-carboxylation of factors II, VII, IX and X, permitting calcium-dependent membrane binding; deficient modification increases bleeding risk.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Heparin directly digests fibrin within an established clot.
Reason: Antithrombin neutralizes activated thrombin and factor Xa.
questions.why: Heparin is an anticoagulant that accelerates antithrombin action, but fibrin breakdown requires plasmin-mediated fibrinolysis.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Platelet dense granules contain ADP and serotonin.
Reason: Platelet alpha granules contain platelet factor 4 and fibrinogen.
questions.why: Both statements are correct but list independent contents of the two platelet granule classes.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about vitamin K and coagulation:
I. Vitamin K supports gamma-carboxylation of prothrombin.
II. Factor XIII is a vitamin K-dependent protease.
III. Citrate enhances calcium-dependent factor binding.
questions.why: Only I is true. Factor XIII is a fibrin-stabilizing transglutaminase, not a vitamin K-dependent protease, and citrate chelates calcium rather than promoting its binding.

questions.stem:
Which statements about coagulation are correct?
I. Factor Xa participates in prothrombin activation.
II. Factor XIIIa cross-links fibrin strands.
III. Platelet phospholipids help organize enzyme complexes.
questions.why: Xa generates thrombin via prothrombinase, XIIIa stabilizes fibrin, and platelet phospholipids support efficient clotting-complex assembly.
